evidence: The recording shows that the burner received the diluted mixture left in the fuel line, not pure propane. At a fuel-controller reading of 0.103 slpm (nitrogen basis) the flame radiated 4.2 V per slpm on the +30 degree radiometer (mean from 4 to 24 s after ignition), against 10.0 in 21301A7, run 4.5 h later at the same setpoint, 9.3 to 11.5 on the 100% propane day 21112 of PSI-159 (same burner, same fuel gas code, 40% O2, 97 kPa; flows of 0.075 to 0.19 slpm) and 5.2 to 5.7 on its 30% propane day 21137. The gas-line pressure above the chamber pressure, 10 s after ignition, was 10.0 kPa per slpm, against 2.5 in 21301A7, 2.3 to 4.1 on day 21112 and 5.6 to 7.4 on day 21137. The chamber pressure rose about half as fast as in 21301A7. The test sheet (AI reading of the hand-filled scan, not checked by a human) gives the cause: a 100% propane bottle was connected, but the fuel line 'had 30% propane (balance N2) before this and wasn't flushed'. fuel_fraction is set to 0.30, the mixture the line held: a nominal value, not a measured composition (the radiometer ratio alone gives 0.2 to 0.3). The table's 1.0 is kept as fuel_fraction_original. 'mfuel (mg/s)' and 'mN2 (mg/s)' in extra were computed for pure propane and are not corrected.
evidence_source: PSI-10 Raw Data 21301A1 and 21301A7_data.csv; PSI-159 Raw Data 21112A1-A6 and 21137A1-A7 _data.csv (channels radiometer3_p30_lo_v, fuel_flow_slpm, outer_coflow_pressure_kpa minus chamber_pressure_kpa); test sheet 'PSI-10_Raw Data_21301 test sheets.pdf' p1 (data/transcriptions/PSI-10/)

evidence: The recording shows the propane fraction rising during this test; no single value describes it. Radiation per unit of fuel-controller flow (0.152 slpm, nitrogen basis; +30 degree radiometer) climbs from 5.0 to 9.7 V per slpm over the 37 s burn. On the 100% propane day 21112 of PSI-159 (same burner, 40% O2, 97 kPa) it is steady at 11 to 12 at the same flow (21112A2), and on its 30% propane day 21137 it is 5.2 to 6.3. The gas-line pressure above the chamber pressure, 10 s after ignition, is 6.3 kPa per slpm (2.3 to 4.1 on day 21112, 5.6 to 7.4 on day 21137). The test sheet (AI reading of the hand-filled scan, not checked by a human) refers to the note on the A1 sheet (patches D51, D52): the fuel line still held 30% propane when the 100% bottle was connected. The fraction went from about 0.3 towards 1.0 while the flame burned; the table's 1.0 is kept and is too high for most of the test.

evidence: How the flames ended, from the ACME test sheets (AI reading of the hand-filled scan, not checked by a human; table test_sheets, column out). The sheets tick one of three endings and agree with the table wherever both speak: all 167 tests ticked 'ext. detect' are self_extinguished in the table, and all 78 ticked 'time out' (54) or 'temp. limit' (24) are flow_terminated. The table's flow_terminated therefore covers two different endings. The 24 temperature-limit tests (21088 F1, 21102 C2, 21102 C5, 21106 F1, 21112A1, 21112 C1, 21112 C2, 21153 A4, 21153 C5, 21174 C5, 21196 M2_1, 21209 A1, 21209 B2, 21242 A1, 21270 A3, 21270 A4, 21270 H2, 21277 A1, 21277 H1, 21277 M1, 21277 N1, 21277 P1, 21291 H2, 21291 J1) were cut off early because the burner got too hot: such a flame neither went out by itself nor lasted the scripted time, and whether it would have gone out is not known. The flag burner_over_limit (peak above 450 C) is not the same set: 22 of the 24 carry it (21102 C5 peaked at 449 C; 21270 A4 at 433 C, and its sheet asks whether it timed out instead), and 8 flagged tests ended otherwise (6 time-outs; 21112 A6 and 21174 C6 went out by themselves).

evidence: How far the uncertain propane fraction of day 21301 reaches, from the recordings. The sheet of 21301A1 (AI reading of the hand-filled scan, not checked by a human) says the fuel line held 30% propane and was not flushed when the 100% bottle was connected. Radiation per unit of fuel-controller flow (+30 degree radiometer, V per slpm on a nitrogen basis, mean from 4 to 24 s after ignition) is 4.2 and 4.3 in A1 and A2, 6.7 in A3 (rising from 5.0 to 9.7 during the burn), 9.3 in A4, 9.5 in A5, 9.4 in A6, and 10.0 to 10.9 in A7, A8, A9, H1, H2 and H3; the references are 9.3 to 11.5 on the 100% propane day 21112 of PSI-159 and 5.2 to 5.7 on its 30% propane day 21137 (same burner, 40% O2). The gas-line pressure agrees: 8.9 to 10.0 kPa per slpm in A1 and A2, 6.3 in A3, 2.5 to 4.3 from A4 on (2.3 to 4.1 on day 21112). So the line was flushed during the third flame, 32 min into the day: A1 and A2 burned about 30% propane (fuel_fraction replaced, D51, D52), A3 a rising mixture and A4 a nearly pure one (flagged, D53, D54), A5 is flagged from its sheet only (D55). 21301A6 to A9 and H1 to H3 (table value 1.0) are not flagged: they are indistinguishable from pure propane within the roughly 5% spread of this comparison. The diluted rows C1, C2, D1, D2, J3 and J4 ran after A6 and give 7.3 to 9.4 V per slpm with nitrogen added, with no sign of a weaker fuel; J1 and J2 have no data file. The sheets of 21301H2 and H3 give fuel flows of 0.092 and 0.082 slpm; the as-run files, the operators' typed notes and the recorded flows (0.079 and 0.089 slpm) say 0.082 for H2 and 0.092 for H3, and so does the table (0.95 and 1.05 mg/s): the two sheets are swapped, the table is right.

evidence: The nine recorded test points missing from the experiment table (note D27) were compared with their recordings and, for seven, with their test sheets (AI reading of the hand-filled scan, not checked by a human). All nine are real ignition attempts that did not give a lasting flame; none is a table row under another id, and no sheet carries a wrong id. 19115D1, 19115C1, 19115H1, 19115P1, 19123H1 and 19175B2: fuel flowed for 3.6 to 7.4 s, the photomultipliers saw light for less than 1.1 s around the igniter, the script stopped on 'EXTINCTION DETECTED' 4 to 8 s after the ignition step, the burner stayed below 80 C and the chamber pressure did not rise; the sheets say 'flash only', 'flashes only', 'No ignition' and, for 19175B2, 'went out immed'. 19123L8: fuel flowed for 12.8 s and the photomultipliers saw nothing; the sheet says 'igniter burn out', so it was an igniter failure, not a test of the flame. The sheet gives 0.052 slpm of nitrogen for 19123L8; none flowed. 19142B1 (fuel for 2.7 s, a flash) and 19196N2 (fuel for 4.9 s, no light at 430 nm) are of the same kind; their days have no test sheets file. The Flame Design tables have no ignition column, and they do list two attempts without a lasting flame (21301J1, J2), so the omission is not a rule of the table. No rows were added for them: the Flame Design rows undercount the ignition attempts by at least these nine.

evidence: The ten recorded test points missing from the experiment table (note D28) were compared with their recordings and their test sheets (AI reading of the hand-filled scan, not checked by a human). None is a table row under another id, and no sheet carries a wrong id. Nine are failed ignitions of day 21106 (butane, 0.5 atm) that the table does not list, although it lists other failures as 'Failed to ignite': 21106A1, A2 and A3 (fuel 0.193 slpm with 0.06 to 0.07 slpm of nitrogen for 13 to 15 s, before 21106A4, about 39% O2; no light on either photomultiplier, no heating), 21106G1 to G5 (after the chamber was refilled to about 21% O2; fuel 0.193 or 0.095 slpm for 14 s, light for 0.1 to 1.8 s around the igniter, burner heating of at most 6 C) and 21106G8 (0.038 slpm; flashes for 1 to 2 s, burner heating of 21 C). The sheets say 'no flame apparent', 'no hot flame apparent' and 'flashes only'. The sheets speak of a 'hot' flame only; whether a cool flame existed cannot be told from these channels. The tenth, 21242F1, is not a test: the recording is 40 s long, no gas flowed and the photomultipliers were never switched on; the sheet says 'IPSU abort before gas flows'. No rows were added. The CFI-G counts of failed ignitions, and the ignition models trained on the table, therefore miss nine failed attempts of day 21106: three at about 39% O2 and six at about 21% O2.

evidence_value: Cygnus OA-6 (free flight after leaving the ISS)
evidence: NASA's catalogue record gives the flight program as 'International Space Station (ISS)', but the same record's hardware field says 'Saffire 1 enclosure in Cygnus' and its approach says 'The Saffire-1 experiments was performed on the Orbital Science’s Cygnus resupply vehicle after it deberthed from the ISS.' The fire burned in the uncrewed Cygnus OA-6 cargo module in free flight, after it had left the station, not on the ISS. The record of SAFFIRE-II (PSI-99) gives 'Cygnus Spacecraft' for the same kind of experiment. The catalogue value is kept in the investigations table (flight_program); the record's `location` (kind cygnus_free_flight) follows the hardware and approach fields.
evidence_source: PSI catalogue record of PSI-98 (fields flightProgram, experimentHardware, approach); 'PSI-98_Science Documents_SAFFIRE Objectives, Development and Status.pdf' p4 (launched within the Cygnus PCM as part of the OA-6 mission)
